floors.label: feature/agenda, excluding Compose-only subtrees
floors.note: The excluded subtrees are Compose-only. They used to be excluded because the per-module report could not see the desktopApp flow tests that cover them, which made the whole scope read 33.18% and said more about the harness than about the tests. The settings-level aggregate now includes those tests, so the exclusion is a choice about what this floor measures, not a workaround — whole scope now reads 76.02%. If the desktopApp task stops running, the excluded subtrees go back to uncovered and this floor will not notice; that is the one reason to keep the exclusion narrow.

floors.label: feature/calendar_sync (per-feature floor)
floors.note:
Dropped from 23.94% to 23.54% on 2026-10-05, and the drop is understood: the background-handler migration replaced two one-line Koin bindings in CalendarSyncDiModule with multi-line ones that compose a failure handler from the injected CrashReportingPort, taking that file from 4/4 to 4/17 lines covered. The 13 uncovered lines are the bodies of `single {}` / `viewModel {}` definitions, which run at *resolution* time, not at module-definition time. KoinGraphValidationTest resolves both definitions for real — and doing so found that the test's own platform mirror was missing a CrashReportingPort binding, which is the defect class this file exists to catch. The coverage number did not move as a result. **The obvious explanation has since been eliminated.** #138's leading hypothesis was that the report came from a `:shared:jvmTest` served `FROM-CACHE` after this recipe's kover wipe — which was true of some runs, and is now prevented by `scripts/check-coverage-measurement.py`. But under `RERUN=1 just cr`, where every test task provably executed, this file still reads 4/17. So the number does describe the run; something about Koin definition bodies is what is not being attributed. Two hypotheses remain, both unexamined: line attribution, and resolution being satisfied without executing the lambda.

**This note is a loan against issue #138 and must be deleted in the same commit that closes it.** It exists so a reader of this floor is not misled into thinking the movement was understood. A hedge written for one reader becomes a permanent mystery for the next.
